rounds.text: IDBI Bank trades at an attractive P/E of 9.52 [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 1.29x [E2], while offering a dividend yield of 2.55% [E4]. This valuation is highly conservative given that the bank's 5-year profit growth of 43% has significantly outpaced its 17% stock price growth, indicating it is potentially undervalued [E48]. A discounted cash flow analysis places the bank's intrinsic value at Rs 354 per share against a market price of Rs 82.4 [E37], which offers a massive margin of safety of 76.7% [E38]. Indeed, a reverse DCF shows that the current stock price implies a -2.2% earnings growth rate, far below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E39]. This market skepticism is unjustified given the bank's superior operational metrics, including an ROA of 2.27% against the sector benchmark of 1.79% [E8] and an ROE of 13.59% against the sector benchmark of 5.11% [E9].

The historical long-term earnings generation power of IDBI Bank Ltd is severely depressed, demonstrated by a dismal median return on equity of -3% over 10 years [E24]. Compounding this structural weakness, the company generates a meager ROCE of just 5.9% [E10], highlighting poor capital efficiency at the core operational level. Furthermore, the bank's recent 3-year return on equity of 13.2% has been officially flagged as a low return [E54], and the valuation reflects a premium price-to-book ratio of 1.47x which exceeds the sector benchmark of 1.36x [E7]. Conceded: the company displays a near-term ROA of 2.27% and an ROE of 13.59% that both outpace their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9].

Conceded: the 10-year median ROE was -3% [E24] and ROCE sits at 5.9% [E10]. However, focusing on a decade-long historical average completely ignores dramatic fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a rising median ROE trajectory that reached 11% over 5 years, 13% over 3 years, and 14% over the last year [E25, E26, E27]. The recent performance outpaces sector benchmarks significantly, with an ROA of 2.27% versus the sector 1.79% and an ROE of 13.59% versus the sector 5.11% [E8, E9]. While the bear highlights a 1.47x P/B ratio against a sector benchmark of 1.36x [E7], filed statements show the actual price-to-book is a modest 1.29x alongside a reasonable P/E of 9.52x [E1, E2]. Furthermore, profit has grown by 43% over 5 years while the price has only risen 17%, proving that fundamentals are outpacing the stock and leaving it potentially undervalued [E48]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price of ₹ 82.4 already prices in a pessimistic -2.2% earnings growth expectation compared to the 18.0% base case [E37, E39].

Conceded: profit has grown by 43% over 5 years while price rose 17% [E48], and the trailing price-to-book sits at 1.29x rather than the slightly higher provider benchmark of 1.47x [E2, E7]. However, the bull's dismissal of the -3% 10-year median ROE ignores a structural track record of severe wealth destruction that a brief recent upswing cannot erase [E24]. That recent 3-year median ROE of 13.2% is explicitly flagged by filed statements as a low return on equity [E54], casting doubt on whether current profitability represents a durable foundation. Furthermore, the reliance on a model-driven reverse DCF implying -2.2% growth ignores the hard reality that ROCE sits at a weak 5.9% [E10, E39]. Finally, trading at 38% of its 52-week range reflects lingering market scepticism regarding sustainability, rendering aggressive terminal assumptions imprudent [E5].
